data.hypothesis: With the existing 128-thread CTA, increasing the source tile from 512 to 1024 lets each CTA process twice as many sources per tile iteration, potentially reducing synchronization and loop overhead. The tradeoff is doubling dynamic shared memory from 8 KiB to 16 KiB and staging eight sources per thread; the controller's full correctness suite and official timing will determine whether this helps.
data.notes: This is one tile-size and compatible launch-configuration experiment. It retains one target and force accumulator per thread, cooperatively stages bounded source data, keeps both barriers unconditional, excludes self-interactions, and writes each active output once. No performance claim is made; measurements are left to the controller.
transformations: Increase the cooperative source tile to 1024 entries and set dynamic shared memory to 16384 bytes, consistent with four 32-bit fields per entry.

Keep the 128-thread launch configuration, one target and accumulator per active thread, bounded partial-tile consumption, global-index self-exclusion, unconditional synchronization, and guarded output coverage.
